arxiv-2102-05024.title: Turkey Behavior Identification System with a GUI Using Deep Learning and Video Analytics
arxiv-2102-05024.creator: Shengtai Ju, Sneha Mahapatra, Marisa A. Erasmus, Amy R. Reibman, Fengqing Zhu
arxiv-2102-05024.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shengtai Ju, Sneha Mahapatra, Marisa A. Erasmus, Amy R. Reibman, Fengqing Zhu. In this paper, we propose a video analytics system to identify the behavior of turkeys. Turkey behavior provides evidence to assess turkey welfare, which can be negatively impacted by uncomfortable ambient temperature and various diseases. In particular, healthy and sick turkeys behave differently in terms of the duration and frequency of activities such as eating, drinking, preening, and aggressive interactions.

arxiv-2211-05588.title: Watching the News: Towards VideoQA Models that can Read
arxiv-2211-05588.creator: Soumya Jahagirdar, Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C. V. Jawahar {soumya.jahagirdar, minesh.mathew}@research.iiit.ac.in dimos@cvc.uab.es jawahar@iiit.ac.in
arxiv-2211-05588.description: Abstract Video Question Answering methods focus on commonsense reasoning and visual cognition of objects or persons and their interactions over time. Current VideoQA approaches ignore the textual information present in the video. Instead, we argue that textual information is complementary to the action and provides essential contextualisation cues to the reasoning process.

arxiv-2401-16417.title: Channel Coding with Mean and Variance Cost Constraints
arxiv-2401-16417.creator: Adeel Mahmood, Aaron B. Wagner
arxiv-2401-16417.description: Abstract We consider channel coding for discrete memoryless channels (DMCs) with a novel cost constraint that constrains both the mean and the variance of the cost of the codewords. We show that the maximum (asymptotically) achievable rate under the new cost formulation is equal to the capacity-cost function; in particular, the strong converse holds.

arxiv-2411-01443.title: Activating Self-Attention for Multi-Scene Absolute Pose Regression
arxiv-2411-01443.creator: Miso Lee, Jihwan Kim, Jae-Pil Heo
arxiv-2411-01443.description: Abstract Multi-scene absolute pose regression addresses the demand for fast and memory-efficient camera pose estimation across various real-world environments. Nowadays, transformer-based model has been devised to regress the camera pose directly in multi-scenes. Despite its potential, transformer encoders are underutilized due to the collapsed self-attention map, having low representation capacity.

arxiv-2504-15193.title: Automated Measurement of Eczema Severity with Self-Supervised Learning
arxiv-2504-15193.creator: Neelesh Kumar, Oya Aran
arxiv-2504-15193.description: Abstract Automated diagnosis of eczema using images acquired from digital camera can enable individuals to self-monitor their recovery. The process entails first segmenting out the eczema region from the image and then measuring the severity of eczema in the segmented region.

arxiv-2506-22636.title: ReCo: Reminder Composition Mitigates Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2506-22636.creator: Sotirios Panagiotis Chytas, Miso Choi, Hyunwoo J. Kim, Vikas Singh
arxiv-2506-22636.description: Abstract Vision Language Models (VLMs) show impressive capabilities in integrating and reasoning with both visual and language data. But these models make mistakes. A common finding – similar to LLMs – is their tendency to hallucinate, i.e., generate plausible sounding text which is not grounded in the visual input, or at worst, is contradictory.

arxiv-2512-09409.title: Proof of Trusted Execution: A Consensus Paradigm for Deterministic Blockchain Finality DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Make sure to enter the correct conference title from your rights confirmation email; June 03–05, 2018; Woodstock, NY ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/06
arxiv-2512-09409.creator: Kyle Habib, Vladislav Kapitsyn, Giovanni Mazzeo, Faisal Mehrban
arxiv-2512-09409.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kyle Habib, Vladislav Kapitsyn, Giovanni Mazzeo, Faisal Mehrban. Current blockchain consensus protocols — notably, Proof of Work (PoW) and Proof of Stake (PoS) — deliver global agreement but exhibit structural constraints. PoW anchors security in heavy computation, inflating energy use and imposing high confirmation latency. PoS improves efficiency but introduces stake concentration, long-range and “nothing-at-stake” vulnerabilities, and a hard performance ceiling shaped by slot times and multi-round committee voting.

pmc-10648512.title: Exosomes Interactions with the Blood–Brain Barrier: Implications for Cerebral Disorders and Therapeutics
pmc-10648512.creator: Zaynab Osaid, Mohamed Haider, Rifat Hamoudi, Rania Harati
pmc-10648512.description: The Blood–Brain Barrier (BBB) is a selective structural and functional barrier between the circulatory system and the cerebral environment, playing an essential role in maintaining cerebral homeostasis by limiting the passage of harmful molecules. Exosomes, nanovesicles secreted by virtually all cell types into body fluids, have emerged as a major mediator of intercellular communication.

pmc-12472221.title: Response of Soil Microbial Communities Between Different Vegetation Types in the Greater and Lesser Khingan Mountains Ecotone in Northeast China
pmc-12472221.creator: Weiping Yin, Xinmiao Guo, Dalong Ma, Huan Yu
pmc-12472221.description: The Greater and Lesser Khingan Mountains ecotone exhibits transitional characteristics between northern coniferous forests and cold-temperate mixed coniferous-broadleaf forests. However, it remains unknown how vegetation characteristics and soil properties jointly influence the structural patterns of soil microbial communities within the forest systems of this ecological transition zone.

pmc-12533096.title: Exploring biases related to the use of large language models in a multilingual depression corpus
pmc-12533096.creator: Paula Andrea Perez-Toro, Judith Dineley, Raquel Iniesta, Yuezhou Zhang, Faith Matcham, Sara Siddi, Femke Lamers, Josep Maria Haro, Brenda W J H Penninx, Amos A Folarin, Tomas Arias-Vergara, Juan Rafael Orozco-Arroyave, Elmar Nöth, Andreas Maier, Til Wykes, Srinivasan Vairavan, Richard Dobson, Vaibha
pmc-12533096.description: Recent advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) present promising opportunities for applying these technologies to aid the detection and monitoring of Major Depressive Disorder. However, demographic biases in LLMs may present challenges in the extraction of key information, where concerns persist about whether these models perform equally well across diverse populations.

pmc-13199798.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of shRNA–IL-6-engineered CAR-T cells for B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia: a stepping stone toward risk-free immunotherapy
pmc-13199798.creator: Mohamed S. Attia, Brett Dyer, Nigel McMillan, Matthew Zunk
pmc-13199798.description: Clinical application of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells, especially those targeting CD19, stands as a breakthrough in treating relapsed or refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Yet, preventing immune-related adverse events, like severe cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS), remains a significant concern. This meta-analysis looked at the efficacy and safety of interleukin-6 knockdown CAR-T therapy.

pmc-13312195.title: Coproducing an intervention to support stroke unit staff to provide information about recovery to patients and carers
pmc-13312195.creator: Louisa-Jane Burton, Thomas Frederick Crocker, Oliver M Todd, Sarah Bates, Anne Forster
pmc-13312195.description: ObjectiveStroke survivors and their carers report receiving insufficient information about recovery, particularly how much is expected and the associated timescales. Providing this information is challenging for stroke unit staff, due to concerns about maintaining patients' hope and motivation for rehabilitation, and a lack of training.

pmc-13396274.title: Loneliness, Depression, and Subjective Memory Complaints in Middle-Aged and Older Adults: The Role of Meaning in Life
pmc-13396274.creator: Seung Chul Lee, Sungkun Cho, Yerin Shim, Dae-Hyun Yun, Taehyun Kim, Soo Rim Noh
pmc-13396274.description: Objective This study examined whether depressive symptoms mediate the association between loneliness and subjective memory complaints (SMCs), and whether meaning in life (MIL) moderates this pathway, among middle-aged and older Korean adults. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 580 adults aged 41–71 years (mean age=58.80; 54.8% males). Participants completed measures of loneliness, depression, SMCs, and MIL.

pmc-13610288.title: Combating Two Major Fungal Diseases in Marigold (Tagetes spp.): Insights into Pathogen Identification and Antifungal Strategies
pmc-13610288.creator: Yi-Ping Zhang, Niaz Ali, Yue-Fei Li, Ci-Lin Yang, Wang-Qi Huang, Feng Xu, Xiu-Mei Yang, Shao-Fang Qian, Zheng-Song Lei, Ji-Hua Wang, Dong-Sheng Tang
pmc-13610288.description: Marigold (Tagetes spp.), a widely cultivated popular ornamental plant that is highly susceptible to fungal diseases, particularly leaf spot and stem wilt, which can substantially reduce its ornamental and economic value. This study aimed to identify the causal pathogens responsible for these diseases and evaluate the efficacy of selected antifungal agents against them.

pmc-13671515.title: Genome-Wide DNA methylation profiling of tissue-plasma pairs identifies Novel cfDNA biomarkers for the diagnosis of gastric cancer
pmc-13671515.creator: Hailing Ou, Jinli Miao, Fusheng Ling, Jie Gao, Tingan Wang, Zhihua Ye, Chunbo Zhang, Mingwei Huang, Yuzhou Qin
pmc-13671515.description: Screening for gastric cancer (GC) is critical for improving patient survival, yet current clinical methods suffer from invasiveness and limited sensitivity. The aim of this study is to develop a machine learning model for the non-invasive diagnosis of GC using the whole-genome methylation profile of circulating free DNA (cfDNA) in plasma.

pmc-13688977.title: Mechanistically resolved prediction of compound hepatotoxicity using primary human liver spheroids—Application to recent real-world cases
pmc-13688977.creator: Yufeng Li, Hongda Sheng, Tingting Zhou, Chen Xing, Miriam Kukasch, Siyuan Shao, Sonia Youhanna, Sabine U Vorrink, Yingxin Liang, Anne T Nies, Julia Dressler, Charlotte Kölz, Jinhye Ryu, Nayere Taebnia, Dominik Jacob, Caroline Hauser, Carl Petersson, Kathrin Klein, Oliver Burk, Boxu Shi, Qiaojun He,
pmc-13688977.description: Drug-induced liver injury remains a major cause of clinical trial attrition and postmarketing drug withdrawals, reflecting persistent translational gaps in predictive preclinical models of compound hepatotoxicity. Here, we applied a well-characterized 3-dimensional primary human liver spheroid platform to interrogate diverse mechanisms of hepatotoxicity and benchmark performance against recent real-world clinical cases.

uslaw-usc-t26-s9002.title: 26 U.S.C. § 9002 — Definitions
uslaw-usc-t26-s9002.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t26-s9002.description: United States Code, Title 26 (Internal Revenue Code); Chapter 95 (Presidential Election Campaign Fund). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. For purposes of this chapter— (1) The term “authorized committee” means, with respect to the candidates of a political party for President and Vice President of the United States, any political committee which is authorized in writing by such candidates to incur expenses.
